question: On 18 November 2025, the Commission imposed safeguard measures in relation to several types of ferroalloys, in response to a surge in imports that is threatening the survival of European producers. However, the safeguard measures were not applied to one specific type of ferroalloy, silicon metal, even though the silicon metal industry has been severely undermined by unfair competition from China.

This material is of major strategic importance for many sectors, including semiconductors, batteries, aluminium, chemistry and defence. European producers of silicon metal face the same serious difficulties as producers of other types of ferroalloys; they are shutting off some of their furnaces, scaling back their activities or even closing down their plants entirely. 1.
Does the Commission recognise the critical situation faced by European silicon metal producers, who have alerted it on several occasions?
Is it prepared to extend the safeguard measures to silicon metal as a matter of urgency, to protect this ferroalloy in the same way as other types?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.4.2026) The Commission acknowledges the critical situation faced by European silicon metal producers and understands their concerns. The Commission opened a safeguard investigation on six manganese- and silicon-based alloys, including silicon metal, in December 20241.

However, the conditions for safeguard measures for silicon metal were not met, as there was no increase in imports. In fact, imports of silicon decreased during the most recent period assessed. Therefore, silicon was not included in the scope of the safeguard measure imposed in November 20252. Nevertheless, the Commission remains attentive to the industry's challenges.

Although the current safeguard measure in force for other ferro-alloys cannot be altered to include silicon, the Commission is committed to exploring all viable options to help the industry, including through trade defence instruments.

The Commission would like to stress that it takes the difficulties of EU silicon metal producers seriously and is continuously engaging with the industry with a view to identifying the most effective way forward.
